item.title: Particle decay, lifetime & width
item.description: Particle Decay, Lifetime & Width The lifetime (or equivalently, the width) and the different ways elementary particles can decay are fundamental properties crucial for physicists exploring the boundaries of known physics.

item.title: ATLAS & LHC Intro Video
item.description: This introductory video to the ATLAS Experiment and the LHC is designed for first-time audiences, offering an accessible introduction to high-energy physics research. It is ideal for educational presentations and public outreach activities. The video is available in multiple languages, with voiceovers recorded by members of the ATLAS Collaboration.

item.title: Inside a Collision
item.description: Inside a Collision Proton collisions at the LHC generate high-energy events, initiating a cascade of processes, such as parton showering and hadronisation, which ultimately produce the particles seen in the ATLAS detector.

item.title: ATLAS Coordinate System
item.description: ATLAS Coordinate System The ATLAS coordinate system allows scientists to accurately and consistently describe how particles travel through the detector.

item.title: Pile-Up
item.description: Pile-Up The LHC collides bunches (groups of protons), which can result in multiple proton-proton collisions at each crossing. Such additional collisions are called pile-up.

item.title: ATLAS Open Virtual Visit
item.description: Join us for an Open ATLAS Virtual Visit, hosted by ATLAS physicists Christian Appelt and Despoina Sampsonidou. This live virtual event will take you inside the ATLAS cavern at CERN, offering a rare opportunity to see the ATLAS detector up close before the cavern is closed for LHC operation. From 100 meters underground, the hosts will guide you around one of the world’s largest and most sophisticated scientific instruments.
